name: Faded Blue
lede: Faded Blue is what a deep blue becomes with wear: washed denim, an old work shirt, a sky-colored cloth that has seen many washings.

sections.title: Worn on purpose
sections.body: Balfour-Paul notes that faded blue work clothes were sometimes chosen deliberately as an anti-establishment statement, most notably blue denim jeans in their early days [1]. Faded blue was, in that sense, a look people picked, not just a result of age [1].

sections.title: Not black, not white
sections.body: Pastoureau writes that Benedictine and Cistercian monks, though shown in true black and white in images, were often dressed in gray, brown or even a more or less faded blue, and that a plain, solid black was a delicate and costly operation on wool [2].

sections.title: The dye behind it
sections.body: Ball titles a section of his chapter on modern colors "Faded blues" and uses it to introduce [[indigo]], which Ball notes was still a natural extract in the 1880s, even then one of the world's major dyestuffs [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #658CBB measures lightness 57.2, chroma 28.8 and hue angle 269 degrees: a mid-light, muted [[blue]], close to a washed [[sky-blue]] [4].
